person.name: Shashi Ramaiah
person.text: Board-certified veterinary pathologist and toxicologist (DACVP, DABT). Spent 18 years at Pfizer, most recently Vice President and Global Head of Discovery, Investigative and Translational Sciences. Founder and CEO of SPECCRO; member of BioCryst's scientific advisory board on rare diseases; speaker on gene therapy (AAV) safety de-risking and on NAMs in drug development.

company.text: SPECCRO is a drug development advisory firm based in Lexington, Massachusetts. It helps biotechnology companies and investors de-risk their programs and portfolios, drawing on a network of 40+ senior experts. Its stated mission is building the infrastructure for NAMs — predictive, human-relevant science instead of animal testing.

posts.text: “Three questions we ask first in scientific diligence”: what target biology predicts about safety, whether the efficacious exposure is reachable without the tox liabilities, and whether the plan reaches a real **decision point with the money being raised**.
posts.use: Mirror his language: Valos's statistics turn those three questions into a clean, defensible data package for investors.

posts.text: “Most programs don't stall on the science. They stall on the sequence.” SPECCRO builds the order of questions with **40+ former large-pharma heads of function**, then runs the CRO work that answers them.
posts.use: Valos fits right after his sequence: when the questions reach the clinic, someone has to analyse the answers.

posts.text: Joined the **BioCryst Pharmaceuticals Scientific Advisory Board** (rare disease), chaired by Tony Manning.
posts.use: Congratulate him — it's his most-liked recent post (76 reactions).

posts.text: Spoke on a panel at **LSX Congress USA (Boston)** about pitching science: “What would kill this programme?” is the first question he asks; “a founder loses my conviction when the deck can't tell me what would kill it.”
posts.use: Open with a candid statement of what Valos does **not** do — he respects naming the weak spot.
